routine.title: Parent-and-tot swim
routine.stage_fit_rationale: Matches the child's interest in water while keeping a caregiver in the pool for safety and comfort, which suits a toddler's need for close supervision and short, structured sessions.

routine.title: Toddler music-and-movement class
routine.stage_fit_rationale: Short, repeated song-and-shaker format fits a toddler's brief attention span and love of movement, while the predictable structure builds comfort through repetition.

routine.title: Neighbourhood park and playground
routine.stage_fit_rationale: Unstructured outdoor time gives a toddler free rein for gross-motor practice like running and climbing, with no schedule pressure so it can flex around naps or mood.

parsed.rationale: A light three-item week spaced across Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday balances one structured water class, one structured movement class, and one free-play outing, matching the toddler's short attention span and need for predictable rhythm without back-to-back demands.
parsed.notes: All three candidates were included since each fits the toddler stage and the stated water/movement interests well; none were dropped, but the mid-week gap (Wed/Fri) is intentional to leave room for naps and unstructured downtime.
